Merge sort, step by step

Merge sort splits the array in halves until each part holds one value, then merges sorted parts back together. A merge only ever compares the front values of two sorted runs.

Click the figure, then use ← →, space, Home and End, or the buttons.

How it works

  1. Split the range at the middle.
  2. Sort the left half, then the right half, the same way.
  3. Merge: compare the front values of both halves and move the smaller into a buffer, drawn under the array.
  4. When one half runs out, add the rest of the other.
  5. Copy the buffer back over the range.

Cost

Time
O(n log n) in every case.
Space
O(n) for the merge buffer.
Stable
Yes: on a tie it takes from the left half first.

The code behind this figure

Nothing here is hand-animated. The figure comes from this code: a plain merge sort with stepthru tracer calls, such as compare and list and set, that record each step.
